commit_subject: (screen-flagged) Subject reads as a new encoding, but the diff rewrites the already-merged module us/regulations/45-cfr/1302/12.yaml: the 10 percent over-income exception is removed from the paragraph_c_participant_eligible OR-chain into a new separate rule paragraph_c_overincome_exception_participant_may_be_enrolled, and the companion test that previously expected paragraph_c_participant_eligible: holds under that path is replaced. PR #461 body says only "Update the generated 45 CFR 1302.12 Head Start eligibility source encoding and companion tests." Unsure whether this is a scope/branch correction or a regeneration; flagged for diff review.
description: Programs may use a 10 percent over-income exception, a 35 percent additional allowance below 130 percent of poverty, Tribal service-area eligibility notwithstanding paragraph (c), and Migrant or Seasonal eligibility based on agricultural employment and age requirements.

release_errors_before_success.error: No active corpus source found for 'us/regulation/45/1302/12'

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix paragraph_c_participant_eligible returned "holds" for an over-income child enrolled under the paragraph (c)(2) ten-percent allowance, but the source says such a family "does not meet a criterion under paragraph (c)(1)" and only permits the program to enroll the child, so a discretionary program-enrollment permission was encoded as a fifth participant-eligibility path.
triage.triage_notes: Provision read through the pinned corpus release (us/regulation/45/1302/12). Decisive source text: "(2) If the family does not meet a criterion under paragraph (c)(1) of this section, a program may enroll a child who would benefit from services, provided that these participants only make up to 10 percent of a program's enrollment in accordance with paragraph (d) of this section." That is an enrollment permission, not eligibility, and it is expressly conditioned on NOT meeting (c)(1); the pre-fix module OR'd it into the eligibility predicate and omitted the family_does_not_meet_paragraph_c_criterion precondition. The post-fix rule name ("..._may_be_enrolled") parallels the existing (d)(1) rule, which is why I kinded this wrong_entity_or_scope (wrong output surface / population) rather than polarity_or_logic (OR-chain fires the wrong branch, fail-open eligibility) or untraceable_branch (branch grounded on (c)(2) but attached to the (c)(1) output) — a reviewer may reasonably prefer either of those two; that kind ambiguity is the main reason confidence is 0.6 rather than higher. SECOND meaning change in the same module, not captured by the single rule_path: report_to_regional_office_required_for_between_100_and_130_percent_enrollment changed its upper bound from `family_income < ... * poverty_line_amount` to `family_income <= ... * poverty_line_amount` (boundary_direction), while additional_allowance_participant_may_be_enrolled keeps strict `<`. That now distinguishes (d)(1)'s "incomes are below 130 percent of the poverty line" (strict) from (d)(2)'s "family incomes are between 100 and 130 percent of the poverty line" (inclusive) — defensible but the inclusive reading of "between" is arguable, so I treated it as secondary. NON-meaning churn in the same diff: dtype Rate -> Decimal on the two multiplier parameters, proof-atom kinds condition -> predicate/formula, removal of local import atoms, commutative reordering of `poverty * multiplier` to `multiplier * poverty`, reworded module summary, and renamed/reworded deferred_outputs entries. PROVENANCE CAVEAT: us/.axiom/encoding-manifests/.../12.json shows a fresh generation (workspace /tmp/axiom-encode-head-start-pe-parity-20260626, codex backend), so this is a regeneration whose output happens to be more faithful, not a maintainer-diagnosed repair; no PR reviews, review comments, or issue comments exist on PR #461 and the PR body is generic ("Update the generated 45 CFR 1302.12 Head Start eligibility source encoding and companion tests."). The quote I used is the module's YAML `summary` prose block added in this diff, not a `#` comment — it is verbatim from the diff. Companion test evidence: the pre-fix case `paragraph_c_ten_percent_benefit_allowance_holds` (income 15000 vs poverty 10000, share 0.1) asserted `paragraph_c_participant_eligible: holds`; the post-fix suite replaces it and asserts `paragraph_c_overincome_exception_participant_may_be_enrolled: holds` instead. Pre-fix module came from PR #441 (5eaffda67); no later commit touches either module file, so the post-fix state is current.
triage.verifier_justification: The diff does change encoded meaning — the (c)(2) ten-percent branch leaves the `paragraph_c_participant_eligible` OR-chain and becomes a separate `paragraph_c_overincome_exception_participant_may_be_enrolled` output — but the evidence does not establish that the pre-fix reading disagreed with the source. The pre-fix rule was grounded on `source: 45 CFR 1302.12(c)` (the whole paragraph, not (c)(1)), the new rule carries the identical `source: 45 CFR 1302.12(c)`, and the source itself at (k)(2)(iii)(D) speaks of a family "determined to be eligible under the criterion in paragraph (c)(2) of this section", so treating (c)(2) as a fifth paragraph-(c) eligibility path is a defensible reading rather than a demonstrated misencoding. Everything else in the diff is regeneration noise (summary rewritten, all five deferred-output ids renamed, proof-atom kinds condition→predicate/formula, all import atoms dropped, dtype Rate→Decimal, multiplication operands flipped, tests rewritten from 2021 to 2024 periods) with a generic message ("Update the generated 45 CFR 1302.12 Head Start eligibility source encoding and companion tests"), and the same regeneration loosened an unrelated bound from `<` to `<=` at 130 percent — a change the source's "incomes are below 130 percent" does not support and which is now inconsistent with the `<` retained one rule above. That pattern points to an uncurated re-encode whose output-granularity split may or may not be a fidelity correction, which is exactly the unclear case.

triage.verifier_notes: Refutation evidence for the reviewer, in priority order. (1) The reader's justifying quote is the module_comment summary, not source text, and its paraphrase "does not meet a criterion under paragraph (c)(1)" is verbatim only in the regulation's (c)(2) conditional: "If the family does not meet a criterion under paragraph (c)(1) of this section, a program may enroll a child who would benefit from services, provided that these participants only make up to 10 percent of a program's enrollment in accordance with paragraph (d) of this section." (resolved via corpus release us-rulespec-foundation-v3-2026-07-15, record 2e094665-d964-54fa-b8d0-94d42cc52236). (2) Counter-text the reader did not weigh: 1302.12(k)(2)(iii)(D) requires the record to state whether "The family was determined to be eligible under the criterion in paragraph (c)(2) of this section" — the regulation itself calls (c)(2) an eligibility criterion, so the pre-fix fifth disjunct is not plainly contrary to the source. (3) Provenance is unchanged: both the pre-fix rule and the new rule declare `source: 45 CFR 1302.12(c)`, so nothing was re-grounded onto a different provision; only output granularity changed. That is why untraceable_branch does not fit; if a reviewer keeps this as a defect, wrong_entity_or_scope (output surface) remains the best kind. (4) Regeneration signals arguing against a curated fix: whole-module summary rewrite, all five deferred_outputs renamed and re-worded, proof atom kinds condition→predicate/formula, every import atom removed, dtype Rate→Decimal on two parameters, commutative operand flips (diff lines 151/152), and the companion test file rebuilt with different period windows (2021→2024), fewer inputs, new names, and an added `auto_positive_migrant_or_seasonal_participant_eligible` case. PR #461 has no reviews, no review comments, and a body that frames the change as "a source prerequisite only". (5) Independent secondary finding worth its own row: at diff lines 182/184 the reporting rule's upper bound moved from `<` to `<=` on 1.30 × poverty line while `additional_allowance_participant_may_be_enrolled` kept `<` at line 152, so a family at exactly 130 percent now triggers regional-office reporting for an allowance it cannot be enrolled under; the source says "whose incomes are below 130 percent of the poverty line" for (d)(1) and only "between 100 and 130 percent" for (d)(2). If anything this is a boundary_direction regression introduced by the regeneration, not a fix. (6) One point in the classification's favor: the new rule adds the source-stated conjunct `family_does_not_meet_paragraph_c_criterion`, which the pre-fix disjunct omitted — though inside the old OR-chain that conjunct was logically redundant, so it changes no pre-fix truth value.
